answers.question: What does it invest in and who runs it?

sentences.text: Kaveri Flexi Cap Fund - Regular Plan - Growth is a Flexi Cap Fund from Kaveri Mutual Fund; its money is 96.5% in shares, 0.0% in debt and 3.5% in cash and similar assets.
It lists 44 companies in its portfolio, and the largest are Reliance Industries Ltd (7.0%), Mphasis Ltd (4.9%) and Radico Khaitan Ltd (4.3%).
It is run by Ananya Rao; the longest-serving manager has been in charge for 7.6 years.

answers.question: How has it done against its benchmark and category over 3, 5 and 10 years?

sentences.text: Over the last 3 years the fund returned 9.0% a year, above its benchmark (Nifty 500 TRI) at 8.4% and below the Flexi Cap Fund average of 9.2%.
Over the last 5 years the fund returned 8.3% a year, above its benchmark (Nifty 500 TRI) at 7.3% and above the Flexi Cap Fund average of 7.9%.
Over the last 10 years the fund returned 12.9% a year, below its benchmark (Nifty 500 TRI) at 13.5% and below the Flexi Cap Fund average of 14.3%.

answers.question: How bumpy has the ride been?

sentences.text: On ₹1.2 lakh, the fund's worst fall of 13.3% would have been about ₹15,355 between its high and its low point.
Over the same dates the worst fall in its benchmark was 14.9%, and the Flexi Cap Fund average worst fall is 15.7%.
It took 195 days from the lowest point to get back to the earlier high.

answers.question: What does it cost per year on your amount?

sentences.text: On ₹1.2 lakh (your holding in this fund) the fund charges about ₹1,986 a year, an expense ratio of 1.7%; the Flexi Cap Fund median for regular plans is 1.6%.
The direct plan of the same fund would charge ₹785 on the same amount, so the regular plan costs ₹1,201 more each year.
The fee is taken out of the fund's value every day, so it is never billed to you separately.
